name: Thomas Crane Public Library

dates.note: The Wikipedia infobox's 'Built' field says 1881; the caption on the same page says 'The original building (1882), front view, architect H. H. Richardson', and a Wikimedia Commons file page read the same day says 'The original building (1882) was designed by H. H. Richardson.' Two dates from one source; neither is edited.

refs.title: Thomas Crane Public Library - Wikipedia
refs.note: Its own judgment, quoted: 'The Thomas Crane Public Library was designated a National Historic Landmark in 1987, recognizing it as one of Richardson's finest library buildings.' It also records that the building 'was funded by the Crane family as a memorial to Thomas Crane, a wealthy stone contractor who got his start in the Quincy quarries.'

note: Written 5 Sep 2026 for WP-11.3, Tranche 2. No HABS survey was found (see the ames-gate-lodge record's note for the query that failed for both). Included because it is the small, cheap, PUBLIC end of the style -- a town library rather than a courthouse or a millionaire's house -- and because the client is the point: the money came from the family of a Quincy stone contractor, in the town whose granite quarries supplied the trade the style depends on. richardsonian-romanesque's own long description makes the availability of skilled stonecutters the style's enabling condition and its death; this building is that argument with a name attached.
